facts.statement: Lehmanosteus is an extinct genus containing only one species of arthrodire placoderm fish.
facts.quote: Lehmanosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm fish

facts.statement: The genus name honors the French paleontologist Jean-Pierre Lehman.
facts.quote: named after French paleontologist Jean-Pierre Lehman

facts.statement: The type species Lehmanosteus hyperboreus was formally described in 1984.
facts.quote: The type species Lehmanosteus hyperboreus was described in 1984

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in the Early Devonian Wood Bay Formation on Spitsbergen, part of the Svalbard archipelago in Norway.
facts.quote: found in Early Devonian strata of the Wood Bay Formation on the island of Spitsbergen, Svalbard in Norway

facts.statement: Lehmanosteus represents one of the most basal members of the order Arthrodira.
facts.quote: It is one of the more basal members of the order Arthrodira

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Lehmanosteus is classified within the class Placodermi.
The animal lived during the Pragian to Emsian stages, between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pragian to Emsian (413.02 to 393.47 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only a single fossil occurrence of Lehmanosteus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
